title: Protocol for Primary Mouse Hepatocyte Isolation
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse.
Cannulate the vena cava.
Perfuse the liver retrogradely through the vena cava to chelate calcium and wash out blood.
Dissect the liver after perfusion.
Perfuse collagenase into the liver to dissociate extracellular matrix.
Purify hepatocytes by density-based separation.
Warm water bath to 42°C.
Place perfusion buffer in the water bath.
Run 70% ethanol through the tubing.
Run air through the tubing for 30–60 seconds.
Wipe the end of the tubing with a paper towel.
Connect 27-gauge needle to the outlet end of the tubing using a luer lock.
Position the anesthetized mouse on the dissection tray.
Cut the mouse fur and skin in a "U" shape.
Move the mouse intestine and viscera to the right.
Reveal the portal vein and vena cava.
Connect the needle to the outlet end of the tubing using a luer lock.
Support the tubing and needle fixture with a heavy object to elevate it from the dissection tray.
Prime the tubing with warm perfusion buffer at a pump speed of 3 mL/min.
Purge some perfusion buffer to wash residual ethanol.
Avoid bubbles in the tubing.
Prepare two 50 mL tubes, one labeled "DB-chilled" and the other "DB-Liberase".
Add 10 mL digestion buffer to each tube.
Keep the tube labeled "DB-chilled" on ice.
Add 250 μL Liberase solution to the tube labeled "DB-Liberase".
Warm the tube labeled "DB-Liberase".
Anesthetize mouse by intraperitoneal injection of anesthesia mix (3.75 μL/g body weight; final concentration for ketamine = 112.5 mg/kg, for xylazine = 22.5 mg/kg).
Place mouse on the edge of the dissection tray and secure limbs using needles.
Wet the fur thoroughly with 70% ethanol.
Make a “U”-shaped incision through the skin.
Secure the skin near the head using a needle.
Move the intestine to the right to reveal the portal vein and vena cava.
Place a stable and heavy object adjacent to the mouse hind legs to support the tubing such that it is slightly higher than the mouse.
Lay the tubing and needle on the object.
Insert the tip of the needle into the vena cava above the kidney, with the bevel side up in an almost flat angle.
Turn on the pump and let the warm perfusion buffer reach the needle.
Insert the needle into the vena cava above the kidney while the buffer is running through the needle.
Monitor for white spots forming in the liver or expansion/swelling of the portal vein.
Insert the needle in a flat angle relative to the vein for cannulation.
Ensure the needle bevel faces upwards during insertion.
Cut the portal vein immediately upon appearance of white spots and/or portal vein swelling (occurs 2-3 seconds after cannulation).
Clamp the portal vein with forceps for 7-10 seconds.
Verify no fluid is passing through when clamping the portal vein.
Check the bottom of the 50 mL tube for bubbles in the tubing.
Clamp the liver before digestion buffer arrives to ensure it swells and relaxes.
Clamp the portal vein every minute during perfusion with no more than 3-4 times.
Dissect out the liver gently after perfusion, lifting central connective tissue between lobes as an anchor point.
Cut all connections of the liver to other organs, remove the gall bladder, place the liver in a tube labeled “DB-chilled,” and put it back on ice.
Clean the pump with ethanol.
Dissect out the liver gently by removing all connections to other organs.
Transfer the liver and media to a 10 cm plate (not pre-coated with collagen).
Rupture the liver sack in a few locations along the surface using fine tip forceps.
Gently release cells using a cell lifter while tilting the plate to submerge the liver in media.
Filter 5 mL of suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube.
Repeat filtering with a new filter and tube for the remaining 5 mL of suspension.
Add another 10 mL of cold plating media to rinse the plate.
Add 5 mL of the rinsing media to each used filter.
Spin at 50 × g for 2 min at 4°C.
Aspirate most supernatant, leaving approximately 1 mL and resuspend the cells by swirling the tube.
Add 10 mL plating media and resuspend by gentle swirling.
Add 10 mL Percoll solution and mix thoroughly by inverting the tube several times.
Spin at 200 × g for 10 min at 4°C with low acceleration and low brake to minimize trauma to hepatocytes.
Aspirate most supernatant, leaving approximately 1 mL and resuspend the cells by swirling the tube.
Add 20 mL plating media. Spin at 50 × g for 2 min at 4°C with low acceleration and low brake to minimize trauma to hepatocytes.
Aspirate supernatant, add 20 mL plating media.
Count viability with a 1:1 dilution trypan blue.
Plate cells according to the specified table.
Place cells in a humidified CO2 incubator.
Pre-warm maintenance media to 37°C.
After 3 h change medium to warm maintenance media.
Keep cells in a humidified CO2 incubator for 16–20 hours.
